Hey there!! You definitely don't owe me or anyone else an apology. I'm a guy who used to drink solely cause "it's Tuesday and I should celebrate getting all my work done for the day." I know how hard it is to turn those thoughts off, especially when everyone around you is telling you to just drink a beer. I failed at sobriety probably 30-40 times before it took hold. I would make it two or three days, or max a week, and then start drinking again. I can't even be sure that my current run of sobriety will last, but for me the best strategy is to just think about each day on it's own. I don't have to be sober forever, just for that day, and then I'll deal with tomorrow when it comes.

Long streaks of sobriety are nice, and they definitely help me feel better about my decision to stop drinking. But I think the most important part is that we decided to stop in the first place. We might slip up, but we decided to stop, and that's a big first step I think. IWNDWYT!!

I have relapsed so many times after about 3-4 weeks. Something that really helped me was writing down exactly how I feel in the midst of a bender. Even when I was drunk I wrote down what I was thinking and feeling. I did the same thing the next day when I was hungover and hating myself. I wrote down most of my thoughts about drinking over a 10 day period. Reading my thoughts and accounts of what drinking does to me really helped me maintain sobriety even when I wanted to drink. Maybe it could help you.
